script.speaker: W1
script.text: Are you going to the study session for the biology midterm tonight?

script.speaker: M2
script.text: I wouldn't miss it for the world.

questions.prompt: What does the man mean?
options: He will not be able to attend.
He has traveled around the world.
He missed the last study session.
questions.key_sentence: I wouldn't miss it for the world.
questions.key_translation_id: Aku nggak bakal ngelewatin itu apa pun yang terjadi.
questions.why_correct_id: **wouldn't miss it for the world** itu idiom yang artinya pasti datang, apa pun yang terjadi. Jadi dia jelas mau ikut sesi belajar.
questions.why_correct_en: **wouldn't miss it for the world** means he will definitely be there.

why_wrong_id.1: Kebalikannya. Ada **wouldn't miss**, artinya nggak mau ketinggalan.
why_wrong_id.2: Jebakan kata **world**. Nggak ada cerita keliling dunia.
why_wrong_id.3: Jebakan kata **miss**. Sesi sebelumnya nggak dibahas.

why_wrong_en.1: The opposite. **wouldn't miss** means he'll be there.
why_wrong_en.2: A trap on **world**. No travel is mentioned.
why_wrong_en.3: A trap on **miss**. No earlier session is mentioned.

questions.analogy_id: Ini kayak bilang nggak akan ngelewatin konser idola, walau dibayar sekalipun.
questions.analogy_en: It's like saying you'd skip your idol's concert for nothing in the world.
questions.tip_id: Idiom yang ada kata negatif kayak **wouldn't miss** sering artinya positif banget. Hati-hati, cuy.
questions.tip_en: Negative-looking idioms like **wouldn't miss** often mean a strong yes.

questions.why_correct_id: **You'd be better off** itu bentuk saran. Sarannya: **taking the shuttle**, naik bus antar-jemput kampus.
questions.why_correct_en: **You'd be better off** is a suggestion: **taking the shuttle**.

why_wrong_id.0: Itu justru masalahnya. Di dekat gedung sains nggak ada tempat parkir.
why_wrong_id.1: Jebakan kata **stadium**. Stadion cuma tempat naik shuttle.
why_wrong_id.3: Izin parkir nggak disebut.

why_wrong_en.0: That's the problem: there's no space there.
why_wrong_en.1: A trap on **stadium**. It's just the shuttle stop.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak saran naik KRL waktu jalanan macet. Masalahnya parkir, solusinya ganti kendaraan.
questions.analogy_en: Like taking the train when the roads are jammed. Problem: parking. Fix: switch rides.
questions.tip_id: **You'd be better off** sama artinya kayak **You should**. Jawabannya kata kerja sesudahnya.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: This printer has jammed again. That's the third time today.

script.speaker: M2

questions.prompt: What does the man mean?
options: He has finished printing his report.
He wants the woman to describe the problem.
He has had similar trouble with the printer.
He thinks the printer has been repaired.
questions.key_sentence: Tell me about it. I lost half my report on it this morning.
questions.key_translation_id: Banget. Tadi pagi setengah laporanku hilang gara-gara printer itu.
questions.why_correct_id: **Tell me about it** itu idiom tanda setuju, artinya aku juga ngalamin. Buktinya laporannya ikut hilang tadi pagi.
questions.why_correct_en: **Tell me about it** means I know exactly. He lost half his report too.

why_wrong_id.0: Kebalikannya. Setengah laporannya hilang.
why_wrong_id.1: Jebakan arti harfiah. Dia nggak minta diceritain.
why_wrong_id.3: Printernya baru macet lagi, jadi belum beres.

why_wrong_en.0: The opposite. Half his report was lost.
why_wrong_en.1: A literal trap. He isn't asking for details.
why_wrong_en.3: It just jammed again, so it isn't fixed.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak temen yang bilang sama, aku juga waktu kamu ngeluh macet. Dia nggak nanya, dia curhat balik.
questions.analogy_en: Like a friend saying same here when you complain about traffic. Not a question, a shared complaint.
questions.tip_id: **Tell me about it** hampir selalu artinya setuju, bukan permintaan cerita.
questions.tip_en: **Tell me about it** almost always means agreement, not a request.

script.speaker: M1
script.text: Professor Hale's statistics lectures move way too fast for me.

script.speaker: W2
script.text: I couldn't agree more. I spend hours rereading my notes.

questions.prompt: What does the woman mean?
options: She finds the lectures easy to understand.
She also has trouble following the lectures.
She does not take notes in class.
questions.key_sentence: I couldn't agree more.
questions.key_translation_id: Setuju banget.
questions.why_correct_id: **I couldn't agree more** artinya setuju banget. Dia juga butuh berjam-jam baca ulang catatan, jadi dia juga susah ngikutin kuliahnya.
questions.why_correct_en: **I couldn't agree more** means total agreement. She struggles too.

why_wrong_id.0: Jebakan kata **couldn't**. Kalimat ini justru setuju penuh.
why_wrong_id.1: Kalau gampang, dia nggak perlu baca ulang berjam-jam.
why_wrong_id.3: Dia baca ulang catatan, jadi dia mencatat.

why_wrong_en.0: A trap on **couldn't**. It's full agreement.
why_wrong_en.1: If it were easy, she wouldn't reread for hours.
why_wrong_en.3: She rereads her notes, so she takes them.

questions.analogy_id: Gelas yang udah penuh nggak bisa diisi lagi. **couldn't agree more** itu setuju yang udah mentok penuh.
questions.analogy_en: A full glass can't hold more. **couldn't agree more** is agreement filled to the top.
questions.tip_id: **couldn't agree more** = setuju. **couldn't care less** = nggak peduli. Dua-duanya sering keluar.
questions.tip_en: **couldn't agree more** = agree. **couldn't care less** = don't care.

questions.why_correct_en: He's never up before eight, so a six o'clock opening doesn't help him.

why_wrong_id.0: Kebalikannya. Jam enam dia masih tidur.
why_wrong_id.1: Jam tutup nggak dibahas sama sekali.
why_wrong_id.2: Nggak ada info dia kerja di kantin.

why_wrong_en.0: The opposite. He's asleep at six.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak warung buka subuh buat orang yang selalu bangun siang. Ya nggak ngaruh.
questions.analogy_en: Like a shop opening at dawn for someone who sleeps till noon. No difference.
questions.tip_id: Jawaban pendek yang ngasih fakta tentang diri sendiri? Tarik kesimpulannya: ngaruh atau nggak buat dia.

script.speaker: M1
script.text: I'm thinking of dropping my art history class.

script.speaker: W2

questions.prompt: What does the woman suggest?
questions.key_sentence: If I were you, I'd talk to the tutor before you make up your mind.
questions.key_translation_id: Kalau aku jadi kamu, aku ngobrol dulu sama tutornya sebelum ambil keputusan.
questions.why_correct_id: **If I were you, I'd** itu bentuk saran. Sarannya ngobrol sama tutor dulu sebelum **make up your mind**, alias memutuskan.
questions.why_correct_en: **If I were you, I'd** is advice: see the tutor before **make up your mind**.

why_wrong_id.0: Kebalikannya. Dia minta nunda keputusan dulu.
why_wrong_id.1: Jebakan kata **tutor**. Yang disaranin ketemu tutor, bukan jadi tutor.
why_wrong_id.2: Jebakan bunyi **make up**. **make up your mind** artinya memutuskan, bukan ujian susulan.

why_wrong_en.1: A trap on **tutor**. See one, not become one.
why_wrong_en.2: A sound trap. **make up your mind** means deciding.

questions.analogy_id: Sebelum buang HP yang lemot, coba bawa ke servis dulu. Siapa tahu masih bisa diselamatkan.
questions.analogy_en: Before tossing a slow phone, take it to a repair shop. It might be saved.
questions.tip_id: **If I were you** = saran. **make up your mind** = memutuskan. Jangan ketipu kata **make up**.
questions.tip_en: **If I were you** = advice. **make up your mind** = decide.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: How was the field trip to the wetlands?

script.speaker: M2
script.text: It would have been perfect if it hadn't rained all afternoon.

questions.prompt: What does the man mean?
options: The weather spoiled part of the trip.
The trip was canceled because of rain.
He enjoyed walking in the rain.
He forgot to bring an umbrella.
questions.key_sentence: It would have been perfect if it hadn't rained all afternoon.
questions.key_translation_id: Bakal sempurna kalau nggak hujan sepanjang sore.
questions.why_correct_id: Conditional (pengandaian) masa lalu ini dibalik faktanya: hujan turun sepanjang sore, jadi nggak sempurna. Tripnya tetap jalan, cuma sebagian rusak karena cuaca.
questions.why_correct_en: Flip the past conditional: it rained all afternoon, so it wasn't perfect. The weather spoiled part of it.

why_wrong_id.1: Tripnya tetap jalan. Dia cerita sorenya hujan, berarti dia ada di sana.
why_wrong_id.2: Kebalikannya. Hujan bikin tripnya nggak sempurna.
why_wrong_id.3: Payung nggak disebut.

why_wrong_en.1: The trip happened; he was there for the rain.
why_wrong_en.2: The opposite. Rain ruined the perfection.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak bilang nasi gorengnya bakal juara kalau nggak keasinan. Tetap dimakan, cuma ada cacatnya.
questions.analogy_en: Like saying the fried rice would be perfect if it weren't so salty. You ate it, but it had a flaw.
questions.tip_id: **would have been... if it hadn't** = kejadian aslinya kebalikan. Hujannya beneran turun.
questions.tip_en: **would have been... if it hadn't** = reality is the opposite. It did rain.

script.speaker: M1
script.text: Do you know if the campus bookstore sells used textbooks?

script.speaker: W2
script.text: It used to, but now it's all new copies.

questions.prompt: What does the woman mean?
options: The bookstore sells only used books now.
She is used to buying new copies.
The bookstore no longer sells used textbooks.
The man should sell his textbooks.
questions.key_sentence: It used to, but now it's all new copies.
questions.key_translation_id: Dulu iya, tapi sekarang semuanya buku baru.
questions.why_correct_id: **It used to** artinya dulu pernah. Lalu **but now it's all new copies**. Jadi sekarang udah nggak jual buku bekas.
questions.why_correct_en: **It used to** means it did in the past. **now it's all new copies**, so no more used books.

why_wrong_id.0: Kebalikannya. Sekarang semuanya buku baru.
why_wrong_id.1: Jebakan bunyi. **used to** di sini kebiasaan toko di masa lalu, bukan **be used to** (terbiasa).
why_wrong_id.3: Nggak ada saran buat jual buku.

why_wrong_en.0: The opposite. It's all new now.
why_wrong_en.1: A sound trap. This **used to** is a past habit, not **be used to**.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak kantin yang dulu jual gorengan, sekarang cuma jual salad. **used to** itu cerita masa lalunya.
questions.analogy_en: Like a canteen that used to sell fried snacks and now sells only salad.
questions.tip_id: **used to** + kata kerja = dulu iya, sekarang nggak. Langsung balik ke kondisi sekarang.
questions.tip_en: **used to** + verb = true then, not now.

script.speaker: W1

questions.why_correct_en: **Not yet**: he's only at the **second interview**, still being selected.

why_wrong_id.0: Itu kabar yang didengar si wanita, tapi si pria membantahnya.
why_wrong_id.2: Dia udah ikut dua wawancara, jadi pasti daftar.
why_wrong_id.3: Dia belum diterima, apalagi kerja di sana.

why_wrong_en.2: He's had two interviews, so he applied.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak lomba lari yang baru lewat setengah lintasan. Belum menang, tapi juga belum kalah.
questions.analogy_en: Like a runner halfway down the track. Not won, not lost.
questions.tip_id: Orang pertama sering salah info. Kalimat orang kedua yang bawa fakta aslinya.

script.speaker: M1
script.text: Would you mind turning the music down a little? I'm trying to study.

script.speaker: W2

questions.prompt: What will the woman probably do?
questions.key_sentence: Oh, sorry. I didn't realize it was that loud.
questions.key_translation_id: Eh, maaf. Aku nggak sadar sekencang itu.
questions.why_correct_id: Si pria minta musiknya dikecilin. Si wanita minta maaf dan bilang nggak sadar suaranya keras. Jadi dia bakal kecilin volumenya.
questions.why_correct_en: He asks her to turn it down; she apologizes. She'll lower the volume.

why_wrong_id.1: Ajakan belajar bareng nggak ada.
why_wrong_id.2: Dia cukup kecilin suara, nggak perlu keluar.
why_wrong_id.3: Masalahnya kekerasan suara, bukan lagunya.

why_wrong_en.3: The issue is volume, not the song.

questions.key_sentence: I've barely scratched the surface.

questions.why_correct_en: **barely scratched the surface** means he's done only a tiny part.

why_wrong_id.0: Kebalikannya. **barely** artinya hampir nggak.
why_wrong_id.2: Jebakan arti harfiah **scratch**, menggores. Bukunya nggak rusak.
why_wrong_id.3: Nggak ada info kelasnya batal.

why_wrong_id.0: Kebalikannya. Si wanita ragu banget.

why_wrong_id.0: Makan setelah kuliah nggak dia tawarin.

why_wrong_id.2: Dia nggak bilang udah makan.

script.text: This afternoon I'd like to talk about one of the strangest sounds in nature: the booming of sand dunes. In about forty deserts around the world, including sites in Morocco, Chile, and California, dunes can produce a deep, low hum that may last for several minutes and be heard more than ten kilometers away. Travelers have described it for centuries, and many believed the sound came from spirits. Today we know the cause is far less mysterious, though scientists still debate the details. The booming happens only when dry sand slides down the steep face of a dune, usually after a person or a gust of wind disturbs the crest. For the sound to occur, the grains must be very round, very dry, and roughly the same size. When millions of such grains move together, they collide in a synchronized rhythm, and the top layer of the dune vibrates like the skin of a drum. Interestingly, each dune tends to have its own note. Researchers who collected sand from different dunes and let it slide in the laboratory found that the pitch depended mainly on the size of the grains, not on the shape of the dune.

script.text: Today we'll look at how the paperback changed reading habits in the twentieth century. Books with paper covers existed long before, but they were usually seen as cheap and badly made. That changed in 1935, when a British publisher named Allen Lane was waiting at a train station after visiting a famous writer. He looked for something good to read on the journey home and found only magazines and poor-quality novels. Lane decided to publish serious books, classics and recent fiction, in paper covers and sell them for about the price of a pack of cigarettes. Other publishers thought he would lose money, because each copy earned so little. Lane's answer was volume. He needed to sell about seventeen thousand copies of each title just to break even, so he looked beyond bookshops. One of his first big orders came from a chain of variety stores, which bought sixty-three thousand copies. Within a year, millions of his paperbacks had been sold. The idea spread quickly to the United States, and during the Second World War, publishers printed millions of small paperbacks for soldiers. By the 1950s, the paperback had made owning books ordinary rather than a luxury.

script.speaker: LEC
script.text: Let's continue our discussion of migration with an insect that seems far too fragile for long journeys: the monarch butterfly. Every autumn, monarchs from eastern North America fly as far as four thousand kilometers to spend the winter in a small area of mountain forest in central Mexico. What makes this trip remarkable is that no single butterfly ever completes the full cycle. The monarchs that fly south in autumn belong to a special generation. Unlike their parents and grandparents, which live only two to six weeks, these butterflies can live up to eight months. They cluster on fir trees through the winter, then begin the trip north in spring. Along the way they lay eggs on milkweed, the only plant their caterpillars can eat, and then they die. Their children and grandchildren continue the journey, and it takes three or four generations to reach Canada. So how do the butterflies find the same forests that their great-grandparents left? Experiments suggest that they use the position of the sun as a compass and correct for the time of day with an internal clock located partly in their antennae.

items.analogy_id: Kata **by** itu kayak tanda tangan pengirim paket. Kalau ada pengirimnya, barangnya dikirim, alias pasif.
items.analogy_en: **by** is the sender's signature. If there's a sender, the thing was sent: passive.
items.tip_id: Lihat **by + pelaku** setelah rumpang? Hampir pasti butuh be + V3.
items.tip_en: See **by + agent**? You probably need be + V3.

items.prompt: ______ she had practiced for months, the pianist felt nervous before the recital.
items.why_correct_id: Habis rumpang ada anak kalimat lengkap: **she had practiced**. Itu butuh conjunction (kata sambung). Maknanya bertentangan, jadi **Although**.
items.why_correct_en: A full clause follows, so it needs a conjunction of contrast: **Although**.

why_wrong_id.0: **Despite** itu preposition (kata depan). Dia cuma bisa diikuti kata benda.
why_wrong_id.1: **In spite** belum lengkap. Harus **In spite of**, dan itu juga kata depan.
why_wrong_id.3: **Because of** kata depan, dan maknanya sebab, bukan pertentangan.

why_wrong_en.1: **In spite** is incomplete and still a preposition.
why_wrong_en.3: **Because of** is a preposition and means cause.

items.analogy_id: Kata sambung itu gandengan yang narik truk lengkap. Anak kalimat **she had practiced** itu truknya.
items.analogy_en: A conjunction is a hitch for a full truck: **she had practiced**.
items.tip_id: Ada pelaku + kata kerja setelah rumpang? Pilih **Although**, bukan **Despite**.
items.tip_en: Subject + verb after the blank? **Although**, not **Despite**.

items.prompt: ______ several reasons why many students prefer evening classes.
items.why_correct_id: Kalimat ini ngenalin sesuatu yang ada, jadi pakai **There**. Bendanya **several reasons**, jamak. Jadi **There are**.
items.why_correct_en: It introduces something that exists, and **several reasons** is plural: **There are**.

why_wrong_id.0: **is** buat tunggal, padahal **reasons** jamak.
why_wrong_id.2: **It is** nggak dipakai buat ngenalin benda jamak yang ada.
why_wrong_id.3: **They are** butuh rujukan sebelumnya, dan di sini nggak ada.

items.analogy_id: **There** itu kayak MC yang ngenalin tamu. Kata kerjanya ngikut jumlah tamu yang masuk.
items.analogy_en: **There** is an MC introducing guests. The verb matches how many come in.
items.tip_id: Kalimat **There is/are**? Lihat kata benda sesudahnya buat nentuin tunggal atau jamak.
items.tip_en: **There is/are**? Check the noun after it.

items.prompt: The engineer ______ designed the new pedestrian bridge received a national award.
items.why_correct_id: Kata yang diterangin **The engineer**, orang. Di anak kalimat dia jadi pelaku **designed**. Pelaku orang pakai **who**.
items.why_correct_en: **The engineer** is a person and the subject of **designed**: **who**.

why_wrong_id.0: **whom** buat objek, padahal di sini dia pelaku.
why_wrong_id.2: **which** buat benda atau hewan, bukan orang.
why_wrong_id.3: **whose** nunjukin kepemilikan dan harus diikuti kata benda.

items.analogy_id: **who** itu seragam khusus orang yang lagi nyetir. **whom** buat orang yang lagi dibonceng.
items.analogy_en: **who** is for the person driving; **whom** for the passenger.
items.tip_id: Setelah rumpang langsung kata kerja? Pakai **who** buat orang, **which** buat benda.
items.tip_en: Verb right after the blank? **who** for people, **which** for things.

items.prompt: Scientists still do not fully understand ______ such long distances each year.
items.why_correct_id: Rumpangnya objek dari **understand**, jadi isinya noun clause (anak kalimat sebagai kata benda). Polanya kata tanya + pelaku + kata kerja, urutan biasa: **why some birds migrate**.
items.why_correct_en: It's a noun clause after **understand**: question word + subject + verb, in statement order.

why_wrong_id.1: **why do some birds** pakai urutan pertanyaan. Di dalam kalimat, urutannya harus biasa.
why_wrong_id.2: Urutannya kacau. Kata tanya harus di depan.
why_wrong_id.3: **that** dan **why** nggak bisa dipakai bareng.

why_wrong_en.1: That's question order, not statement order.

items.analogy_id: Pertanyaan yang masuk ke dalam kalimat itu kayak tamu yang udah duduk. Dia nggak berdiri lagi kayak pas nanya.
items.analogy_en: A question inside a sentence is a guest who has sat down; it's not standing to ask anymore.
items.tip_id: Kata tanya di tengah kalimat? Jangan pakai **do/does/did**. Langsung pelaku + kata kerja.
items.tip_en: Question word mid-sentence? No **do/does/did**.

items.prompt: The second edition of the textbook is ______ the first, with clearer diagrams and fewer errors.
items.why_correct_id: Ada dua edisi yang dibandingin, jadi pakai comparative (bentuk lebih) + **than**. **much** boleh nguatin. Jadi **much better than**.
items.why_correct_en: Two editions compared: comparative + **than**, with **much** as an intensifier.

why_wrong_id.0: **more better** itu dobel. **better** udah bentuk lebih.
why_wrong_id.1: **the best** buat tiga atau lebih, dan butuh **of** grup.
why_wrong_id.3: Comparative pasangannya **than**, bukan **as**.

why_wrong_en.1: **the best** is for three or more.

items.analogy_id: **better** itu udah naik satu lantai. Tambah **more** sama aja naik lift yang udah sampai.
items.analogy_en: **better** is already one floor up. Adding **more** rides a lift that has arrived.
items.tip_id: Dua benda dibandingin? Cari **-er than** atau **more ... than**. Jangan dobel.
items.tip_en: Two things? **-er than** or **more ... than**, never both.

items.prompt: Rarely ______ such a large crowd at a public lecture on mathematics.
items.why_correct_id: **Rarely** di awal kalimat bikin inversi (urutan dibalik). Kata bantu **has** maju ke depan pelaku: **has the hall seen**.
items.why_correct_en: **Rarely** at the start triggers inversion: **has the hall seen**.

why_wrong_id.0: Urutan biasa. Setelah **Rarely**, harus dibalik.
why_wrong_id.1: Yang maju cuma kata bantu, bukan **seen**.
why_wrong_id.2: **seeing** bukan kata kerja lengkap.

items.analogy_id: Kata negatif di depan itu kayak bunyi sirene. Kernet **has** langsung loncat ke depan buat buka jalan.
items.analogy_en: A negative word up front is a siren. The helper **has** jumps ahead.
items.tip_id: **Rarely, Seldom, Never, Hardly** di awal = kata bantu + pelaku.
items.tip_en: **Rarely, Seldom, Never** up front = helper + subject.

items.prompt: The committee agreed ______ the proposal at its next meeting.
items.why_correct_id: Kata kerja **agree** selalu diikuti **to + V1**. Jadi **agreed to discuss**.
items.why_correct_en: **agree** takes **to + verb**: **agreed to discuss**.

why_wrong_id.0: **agree** nggak diikuti -ing.
why_wrong_id.1: Dua kata kerja nggak bisa nempel langsung tanpa **to**.
why_wrong_id.3: **discussed** bikin dua kata kerja lampau berderet.

why_wrong_en.1: Two verbs can't sit together without **to**.
why_wrong_en.3: Two past verbs in a row.

items.analogy_id: **agree, decide, plan, hope** itu geng **to**. Mereka selalu jalan bareng **to**.
items.analogy_en: **agree, decide, plan, hope** always travel with **to**.
items.tip_id: Hafalin geng **to**: agree, decide, plan, hope, refuse, promise.
items.tip_en: Learn the **to** crew: agree, decide, plan, hope, refuse, promise.

items.prompt: ______ by a volcanic eruption thousands of years ago, the island now supports dense tropical forests.
items.why_correct_id: Pelaku kalimat utamanya **the island**. Pulau itu dibentuk oleh letusan, jadi maknanya pasif. Bentuk pendeknya V3: **Formed**.
items.why_correct_en: **the island** was formed by an eruption: passive, reduced to **Formed**.

why_wrong_id.0: **Forming** aktif: pulaunya yang membentuk sesuatu.
why_wrong_id.2: **It was formed** bikin dua kalimat lengkap tanpa kata sambung.
why_wrong_id.3: **Having formed it** aktif dan punya objek yang nggak jelas.

why_wrong_en.2: Two full clauses with no connector.

items.analogy_id: Pulau itu kayak kue yang dicetak. Kuenya nggak nyetak, dia dicetak: **Formed**.
items.analogy_en: The island is a cake from a mold. It didn't mold; it was molded.
items.tip_id: Frasa pembuka sebelum koma? Cek pelaku utama: dia yang melakukan (-ing) atau dikenai (V3)?
items.tip_en: Opening phrase? Does the main subject act (-ing) or receive (V3)?

items.prompt: The scholarship is open to students who are either enrolled full-time ______ working as teaching assistants.
items.why_correct_id: Ada **either** sebelumnya. Pasangan **either** selalu **or**. Jadi **either enrolled... or working**.
items.why_correct_en: **either** always pairs with **or**.

why_wrong_id.0: **nor** pasangannya **neither**.
why_wrong_id.2: **and** pasangannya **both**.
why_wrong_id.3: **but also** pasangannya **not only**.

items.analogy_id: Pasangan kata ini kayak sepatu kiri dan kanan. **either** cuma cocok sama **or**.
items.analogy_en: These pairs are left and right shoes. **either** fits only **or**.
items.tip_id: Hafalin pasangannya: either-or, neither-nor, both-and, not only-but also. Aman.
items.tip_en: either-or, neither-nor, both-and, not only-but also.

items.prompt: Students who lose their ID cards must ______ the security office immediately.
items.why_correct_id: Setelah modal (kata kerja bantu kemampuan atau keharusan) **must**, kata kerjanya selalu V1. Jadi **notify**.
items.why_correct_en: After the modal **must**, use the base verb: **notify**.

why_wrong_id.0: Modal nggak diikuti -ing.
why_wrong_id.2: Modal nggak diikuti **to**.
why_wrong_id.3: Modal nggak diikuti V2 atau V3.

why_wrong_en.3: No past form after a modal.

items.analogy_id: Modal itu kayak colokan yang cuma muat satu jenis steker: V1.
items.analogy_en: A modal is a socket that fits one plug: the base verb.
items.tip_id: Habis **must, can, will, should**? Langsung V1 polos.
items.tip_en: After **must, can, will, should**: base verb.

items.prompt: The experiment had to be repeated ______ the first set of samples was contaminated.
items.why_correct_id: Setelah rumpang ada anak kalimat lengkap: **the first set of samples was contaminated**. Butuh kata sambung sebab: **because**.
items.why_correct_en: A full clause follows, and it gives a reason: **because**.

why_wrong_id.1: **because of** kata depan, cuma buat kata benda.
why_wrong_id.2: **due to** juga kata depan.
why_wrong_id.3: **so that** artinya supaya, maknanya tujuan, bukan sebab.

items.analogy_id: **because** itu jembatan buat mobil lengkap. **because of** cuma buat pejalan kaki, alias kata benda.
items.analogy_en: **because** carries a full car; **because of** carries a pedestrian (a noun).
items.tip_id: Pelaku + kata kerja sesudahnya? **because**. Cuma kata benda? **because of**.
items.tip_en: Clause after it? **because**. Noun only? **because of**.

items.prompt: The librarian gave the new students ______ helpful information about the online catalog.
items.why_correct_id: **information** itu uncountable (nggak bisa dihitung). Yang cocok buat benda nggak terhitung: **some**.
items.why_correct_en: **information** is uncountable, so **some** fits.

why_wrong_id.1: **many** buat benda jamak yang bisa dihitung.
why_wrong_id.2: **a** cuma buat benda tunggal yang bisa dihitung.
why_wrong_id.3: **a few** juga buat benda yang bisa dihitung.

items.analogy_id: **information** itu kayak air, bukan kelereng. Air nggak bisa dihitung satu, dua, tiga.
items.analogy_en: **information** is water, not marbles. You can't count it.
items.tip_id: Hafalin uncountable yang sering keluar: advice, information, equipment, research, furniture.
items.tip_en: Common uncountables: advice, information, equipment, research, furniture.

items.prompt: By the time the rescue team arrived, the climbers ______ on the ledge for nearly two days.
items.why_correct_id: **By the time** + lampau nunjukin kejadian yang udah berlangsung sebelum titik lampau itu. Plus ada lamanya **for nearly two days**. Jadi past perfect continuous: **had been waiting**.
items.why_correct_en: **By the time** + past, with a duration: **had been waiting**.

why_wrong_id.1: **have waited** itu masa kini, nggak cocok sama **arrived**.
why_wrong_id.2: **were wait** salah bentuk. Harusnya **were waiting**.
why_wrong_id.3: **are waiting** masa kini, padahal ceritanya lampau.

why_wrong_en.3: Present tense in a past story.

items.analogy_id: Kayak jam pasir. Pasirnya udah turun dua hari waktu tim datang. Itu **had been waiting**.
items.analogy_en: Like an hourglass that had run for two days when the team arrived.
items.tip_id: **By the time** + V2? Kejadian yang lebih dulu pakai **had**.
items.tip_en: **By the time** + past? The earlier event takes **had**.

items.prompt: The {A}results{/A} of the national survey {B}was{/B} published {C}in{/C} a {D}leading{/D} journal last month.
items.why_correct_id: Pelaku aslinya **The results**, jamak. Frasa **of the national survey** cuma tempelan. Jadi harus **were published**.
items.why_correct_en: The real subject is **The results**, plural, so **were published**.

why_wrong_id.0: **results** jamak dan pas jadi pelaku.
why_wrong_id.2: **in a journal** itu kata depan yang pas buat terbitan.
why_wrong_id.3: **leading** itu adjective (kata sifat) yang artinya terkemuka. Aman.

items.analogy_id: Frasa **of** itu kayak gerbong tambahan. Yang nentuin arah tetap lokomotifnya: **results**.
items.analogy_en: The **of** phrase is an extra carriage. The engine, **results**, sets the verb.
items.tip_id: Lihat frasa **of** setelah pelaku? Coret dulu, baru cek kata kerjanya.
items.tip_en: Cross out the **of** phrase, then check the verb.

items.prompt: The {A}decide{/A} to close the old laboratory {B}was made{/B} after {C}a long{/C} {D}discussion{/D} among the staff.
items.why_correct_id: Setelah **The**, posisinya harus noun (kata benda). **decide** itu kata kerja. Bentuk bendanya **decision**.
items.why_correct_en: After **The** you need a noun: **decision**, not **decide**.

why_wrong_id.1: Keputusan itu dibuat, jadi pasif **was made** pas.
why_wrong_id.2: **a long** + kata benda tunggal. Aman.
why_wrong_id.3: **discussion** kata benda setelah kata sifat **long**. Pas.

why_wrong_en.1: A decision is made: passive fits.

items.analogy_id: Slot setelah **The** itu parkiran khusus kata benda. Kata kerja nggak boleh parkir di situ.
items.analogy_en: The slot after **The** is noun-only parking.
items.tip_id: **The** + ___ + **to/of**? Cek akhiran benda: -sion, -tion, -ment.
items.tip_en: **The ___ to/of**? Look for -sion, -tion, -ment.

items.prompt: The position requires {A}organizing{/A} campus events, {B}answering{/B} student emails, and {C}to manage{/C} the club {D}budget{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: Ada daftar tiga tugas. Dua yang pertama pakai -ing: **organizing**, **answering**. Biar sejajar, yang ketiga juga harus **managing**.
items.why_correct_en: The list uses -ing: **organizing**, **answering**, so **managing**.

why_wrong_id.0: **requires** + -ing itu pola yang pas.
why_wrong_id.1: **answering** sejajar sama **organizing**.
why_wrong_id.3: **budget** itu kata benda objek. Aman.

items.analogy_id: Daftar itu kayak barisan seragam. Satu orang pakai baju beda langsung kelihatan.
items.analogy_en: A list is a uniformed line. One different outfit stands out.
items.tip_id: Lihat **and** di akhir daftar? Samain bentuk semua anggotanya.
items.tip_en: See **and** ending a list? Match every item.

items.prompt: The ancient manuscript was {A}so{/A} fragile {B}that{/B} the researchers {C}had to{/C} handle it {D}extreme{/D} carefully.
items.why_correct_id: Yang diterangin di sini **carefully**, adverb (kata keterangan). Yang nerangin adverb juga harus adverb. Jadi **extremely carefully**.
items.why_correct_en: It modifies the adverb **carefully**, so it must be an adverb: **extremely**.

why_wrong_id.0: **so ... that** itu pasangan sebab-akibat yang pas.
why_wrong_id.1: **that** melengkapi **so fragile**.
why_wrong_id.2: **had to** + V1 itu pola keharusan lampau.

items.analogy_id: Adverb itu gaya nyetir. Kalau mau bilang nyetirnya super hati-hati, kata penguatnya juga harus gaya nyetir.
items.analogy_en: An adverb is a driving style. To intensify it, you need another style word.
items.tip_id: Kata sebelum kata ber-ly? Biasanya juga harus ber-ly.
items.tip_en: A word before an -ly word usually needs -ly too.

items.prompt: {A}Them{/A} who finish the exam early {B}may{/B} leave the room {C}quietly{/C} {D}after{/D} handing in their papers.
items.why_correct_id: **Them** itu pronoun (kata ganti) bentuk objek. Di sini dia jadi pelaku yang diterangin **who**. Polanya **Those who**.
items.why_correct_en: **Them** is an object pronoun. The subject pattern is **Those who**.

why_wrong_id.1: **may** + V1 **leave** pas buat izin.
why_wrong_id.2: **quietly** adverb yang nerangin **leave**. Aman.
why_wrong_id.3: **after** + -ing **handing** itu pola yang bener.

items.analogy_id: **Them** itu penumpang, nggak boleh pegang setir. Yang nyetir di depan **who** harus **Those**.
items.analogy_en: **Them** is a passenger; it can't drive. Before **who**, use **Those**.
items.tip_id: Pelaku yang diikuti **who**? Pakai **Those who**, bukan **Them who**.
items.tip_en: Subject + **who**? **Those who**.

items.prompt: Since 2010, the city {A}has{/A} {B}build{/B} more than forty {C}new{/C} parks {D}in{/D} its poorer neighborhoods.
items.why_correct_id: Setelah **has**, kata kerjanya harus V3. **build** itu V1. V3-nya **built**.
items.why_correct_en: After **has**, use V3: **built**.

why_wrong_id.0: **Since 2010** cocok sama present perfect, jadi **has** pas.
why_wrong_id.2: **new** kata sifat buat **parks**. Aman.
why_wrong_id.3: **in its neighborhoods** kata depan tempat yang pas.

items.analogy_id: **has** itu kernet yang cuma nerima penumpang V3. **build** belum ganti baju jadi **built**.
items.analogy_en: **has** only lets V3 board. **build** must change into **built**.
items.tip_id: Ada **has/have/had**? Langsung cek kata kerja berikutnya: udah V3 belum?
items.tip_en: **has/have/had**? Check for V3 next.

items.prompt: The ancient city of Petra, {A}which{/A} was carved {B}into{/B} rose-colored cliffs, {C}it{/C} attracts {D}nearly{/D} a million visitors a year.
items.why_correct_id: Pelakunya udah ada: **The ancient city of Petra**. Anak kalimat **which...** cuma sisipan. **it** jadi pelaku dobel, jadi harus dibuang.
items.why_correct_en: The subject is **Petra**; **it** repeats it. Remove **it**.

why_wrong_id.0: **which** pas buat nerangin tempat.
why_wrong_id.1: **carved into** artinya dipahat ke dalam. Pas.
why_wrong_id.3: **nearly** nerangin angka. Aman.

items.analogy_id: Satu mobil, satu sopir. **it** itu sopir kedua yang nyelonong.
items.analogy_en: One car, one driver. **it** is a second driver.
items.tip_id: Pelaku + koma + sisipan + koma? Setelah koma kedua langsung kata kerja, tanpa pelaku baru.
items.tip_en: Subject, insert, then the verb directly.

items.prompt: She hopes to become {A}an{/A} university professor {B}after{/B} {C}completing{/C} her {D}doctorate{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: Article (kata sandang) **a/an** ditentukan bunyi, bukan huruf. **university** dibaca **yu-ni**, bunyinya konsonan. Jadi **a university**.
items.why_correct_en: **university** starts with a consonant sound, so **a**.

why_wrong_id.1: **after** + -ing pas.
why_wrong_id.2: **completing** -ing setelah kata depan. Aman.
why_wrong_id.3: **doctorate** kata benda setelah **her**. Pas.

items.analogy_id: **a/an** itu kayak pintu otomatis yang dengerin suara, bukan lihat tulisan. **yu** kedengeran konsonan.
items.analogy_en: **a/an** listens to sound, not spelling. **yu** sounds like a consonant.
items.tip_id: Waspada kata yang dibuka bunyi **yu** atau **h** bisu: a university, an hour.
items.tip_en: Watch **yu** sounds and silent **h**: a university, an hour.

items.prompt: Unlike most mammals, the platypus lays eggs and is {A}capable{/A} {B}to detect{/B} electric fields {C}with{/C} {D}its{/D} bill.
items.why_correct_id: **capable** pasangannya **of** + -ing. Jadi **capable of detecting**, bukan **capable to detect**.
items.why_correct_en: **capable** takes **of** + -ing: **capable of detecting**.

why_wrong_id.0: **capable** kata sifat yang pas setelah **is**.
why_wrong_id.2: **with its bill** artinya pakai paruhnya. Kata depan pas.
why_wrong_id.3: **its** tunggal buat **the platypus**. Aman.

items.analogy_id: Beberapa kata sifat punya pasangan tetap. **capable** cuma mau dansa sama **of**.
items.analogy_en: Some adjectives have fixed partners. **capable** dances only with **of**.
items.tip_id: Hafalin: capable of, able to, interested in, responsible for.
items.tip_en: capable of, able to, interested in, responsible for.

items.prompt: Because of the drought, farmers in the region harvested {A}far{/A} {B}less{/B} corn this year and had {C}to buy{/C} {D}much{/D} bags of feed.
items.why_correct_id: **bags** itu benda jamak yang bisa dihitung. Buat yang bisa dihitung pakai **many**, bukan **much**.
items.why_correct_en: **bags** is countable plural: **many**, not **much**.

why_wrong_id.0: **far** nguatin perbandingan **less**. Aman.
why_wrong_id.1: **corn** nggak bisa dihitung, jadi **less** pas.
why_wrong_id.2: **had to** + V1 itu keharusan lampau.

items.analogy_id: Karung bisa dihitung satu-satu kayak kelereng. Jagung curah kayak air, pakai **less**.
items.analogy_en: Bags are marbles you can count; loose corn is water.
items.tip_id: Kata benda ber-s di belakang? Pakai **many** atau **fewer**.
items.tip_en: Plural -s noun? **many** or **fewer**.

items.prompt: Last summer, the research team {A}traveled{/A} to Greenland, where they {B}measured{/B} the ice and {C}taken{/C} samples {D}from{/D} several glaciers.
items.why_correct_id: **measured** dan kata kerja kedua disambung **and**, jadi harus sama-sama V2. **taken** itu V3 tanpa **have**. Yang bener **took**.
items.why_correct_en: **measured and ...** needs a past verb: **took**, not **taken**.

why_wrong_id.0: **Last summer** cocok sama V2 **traveled**.
why_wrong_id.1: **measured** V2 yang pas.
why_wrong_id.3: **samples from glaciers** kata depan asal. Aman.

items.analogy_id: V3 kayak penumpang yang butuh tiket **have**. Tanpa tiket, dia nggak boleh naik.
items.analogy_en: V3 needs a **have** ticket. Without it, no ride.
items.tip_id: V3 sendirian tanpa **have/be**? Hampir pasti salah.
items.tip_en: A lone V3 with no **have/be** is a red flag.

items.prompt: Not until the late 1800s {A}scientists understood{/A} that many diseases {B}are{/B} spread {C}by{/C} microscopic {D}organisms{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: **Not until** di awal kalimat bikin inversi (urutan dibalik). Polanya **did + pelaku + V1**: **did scientists understand**.
items.why_correct_en: **Not until** at the start needs inversion: **did scientists understand**.

why_wrong_id.1: Fakta umum, jadi present **are spread** pas.
why_wrong_id.2: **by** nunjukin pelaku pasif.
why_wrong_id.3: **organisms** jamak setelah **microscopic**. Aman.

items.analogy_id: **Not until** itu palang pintu. Kernet **did** harus maju duluan buat buka palangnya.
items.analogy_en: **Not until** is a gate; **did** must step forward first.
items.tip_id: Kalimat dibuka **Not until, Only after, Never**? Cari inversi setelah keterangan waktunya.
items.tip_en: **Not until, Only after, Never**: invert after the time phrase.

items.prompt: Every one of the paintings {A}in{/A} the exhibition {B}have been{/B} {C}carefully{/C} restored {D}by{/D} experts.
items.why_correct_id: Pelakunya **Every one**, tunggal. Jadi kata kerjanya **has been**, bukan **have been**.
items.why_correct_en: **Every one** is singular: **has been**.

why_wrong_id.0: **in the exhibition** kata depan tempat. Aman.
why_wrong_id.2: **carefully** adverb yang nerangin **restored**.
why_wrong_id.3: **by experts** nunjukin pelaku pasif.

items.analogy_id: **Every one** itu kayak satu tiket buat satu orang. Walau penontonnya ribuan, tiketnya satu-satu.
items.analogy_en: **Every one** is one ticket per person.
items.tip_id: **Every one of, Each of, One of** = tunggal. Jangan ketipu kata jamak setelah **of**.
items.tip_en: **Every one of, Each of, One of** = singular.

items.prompt: The climate of northern Canada is {A}much{/A} colder {B}than{/B} {C}southern Canada{/C}, {D}especially{/D} in January.
items.why_correct_id: Yang dibandingin itu **The climate**. Jadi lawannya juga harus iklim: **that of southern Canada**. Sekarang malah iklim dibandingin sama wilayah.
items.why_correct_en: It compares **The climate** with a region. It should be **that of southern Canada**.

why_wrong_id.0: **much** nguatin **colder**. Aman.
why_wrong_id.1: **colder than** pasangan yang pas.
why_wrong_id.3: **especially** adverb yang nerangin **in January**.

items.analogy_id: Bandingin apel sama apel. Iklim lawan iklim, bukan iklim lawan peta.
items.analogy_en: Compare apples with apples: climate with climate.
items.tip_id: Perbandingan diawali **The ... of**? Cek lawannya pakai **that of** atau **those of**.
items.tip_en: Starts with **The ... of**? The other side needs **that of**.

items.prompt: Visitors to the archive {A}must{/A} {B}wear{/B} gloves and {C}should{/C} never {D}touching{/D} the documents with bare hands.
items.why_correct_id: Setelah modal **should** (dan **never**), kata kerjanya harus V1. Jadi **should never touch**.
items.why_correct_en: After **should**, use the base verb: **touch**.

why_wrong_id.0: **must** modal yang pas.
why_wrong_id.1: **must wear** V1 setelah modal. Aman.
why_wrong_id.2: **should** modal yang pas buat larangan.

items.analogy_id: **never** cuma numpang lewat. Modal tetap minta V1 polos.
items.analogy_en: **never** is just passing through. The modal still wants a base verb.
items.tip_id: Ada kata di antara modal dan kata kerja? Lompati, lalu cek kata kerjanya V1.
items.tip_en: Skip words between the modal and verb; check the base form.

items.prompt: The biologist {A}which{/A} discovered the new species {B}spent{/B} three years {C}studying{/C} the forests {D}of{/D} Borneo.
items.why_correct_id: **The biologist** itu orang. Kata penghubung buat orang **who**, bukan **which**.
items.why_correct_en: A biologist is a person: **who**, not **which**.

why_wrong_id.1: **spent** V2 yang pas buat kalimat lampau.
why_wrong_id.2: **spend + waktu + -ing**. Aman.
why_wrong_id.3: **the forests of Borneo** kata depan kepemilikan. Pas.

items.analogy_id: **which** itu stiker buat barang. Orang dapat stiker **who**.
items.analogy_en: **which** is a label for things; people get **who**.
items.tip_id: Kata benda orang sebelum relative clause (anak kalimat penjelas)? Pakai **who/whom/whose**.
items.tip_en: Person before the clause? **who/whom/whose**.

items.prompt: When the fire alarm rang yesterday, the students {A}calmly{/A} {B}leave{/B} the building {C}and{/C} gathered {D}in{/D} the parking lot.
items.why_correct_id: Ceritanya lampau: **rang yesterday** dan **gathered**. Jadi **leave** harus **left**.
items.why_correct_en: It's past: **rang** and **gathered**, so **left**.

why_wrong_id.0: **calmly** adverb yang nerangin cara keluar.
why_wrong_id.2: **and** nyambungin dua kata kerja.
why_wrong_id.3: **in the parking lot** kata depan tempat.

items.analogy_id: Semua kata kerja dalam satu cerita itu satu rombongan. Satu yang beda zaman langsung ketahuan.
items.analogy_en: Verbs in one story travel together. One from another time stands out.
items.tip_id: Ada **yesterday, last, ago**? Semua kata kerja di cerita itu V2.
items.tip_en: **yesterday, last, ago**? All past.

items.prompt: The {A}growing{/A} demand for electric cars has led to a {B}sharp{/B} increase in the {C}produce{/C} of lithium {D}batteries{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: Pola **the ___ of** butuh kata benda yang artinya proses membuat. **produce** di sini salah. Yang pas **production**.
items.why_correct_en: **the ___ of** needs the process noun: **production**.

why_wrong_id.0: **growing** kata sifat buat **demand**. Aman.
why_wrong_id.1: **sharp** kata sifat buat **increase**. Pas.
why_wrong_id.3: **batteries** jamak, benda yang diproduksi.

items.analogy_id: **production** itu pabriknya, **produce** itu hasil kebunnya. Di sini yang dimaksud pabrik.
items.analogy_en: **production** is the factory process; **produce** is farm goods.
items.tip_id: **the ___ of** + barang? Cari akhiran -tion atau -ment.
items.tip_en: **the ___ of**? Try -tion or -ment.

items.prompt: The team continued the expedition {A}in spite of{/A} the storm, {B}and{/B} they returned safely {C}two days later{/C} {D}because of{/D} the weather had improved.
items.why_correct_id: Setelah bagian D ada anak kalimat lengkap: **the weather had improved**. Itu butuh kata sambung **because**, bukan kata depan **because of**.
items.why_correct_en: A full clause follows, so **because**, not **because of**.

why_wrong_id.0: **in spite of the storm** kata depan + kata benda. Pas.
why_wrong_id.1: **and** nyambungin dua kalimat lengkap.
why_wrong_id.2: Keterangan waktu yang wajar.

items.analogy_id: **because of** cuma kuat narik koper, alias kata benda. Anak kalimat itu truk, butuh **because**.
items.analogy_en: **because of** pulls a suitcase; a clause is a truck that needs **because**.
items.tip_id: Cek kata setelah **because of/despite**: kalau ada kata kerja, itu salah.
items.tip_en: A verb after **because of/despite** is wrong.

items.prompt: Most students look forward {A}to receive{/A} their exam results, {B}although{/B} some {C}prefer{/C} {D}not to{/D} know immediately.
items.why_correct_id: **look forward to** itu frasa tetap, dan **to**-nya kata depan. Setelah kata depan harus -ing. Jadi **to receiving**.
items.why_correct_en: In **look forward to**, **to** is a preposition: **to receiving**.

why_wrong_id.1: **although** + anak kalimat lengkap. Pas.
why_wrong_id.2: **some prefer** pelaku jamak + V1. Aman.
why_wrong_id.3: **prefer not to know** pola yang bener.

items.analogy_id: **to** di sini nyamar. Kelihatannya **to** infinitive, padahal kata depan yang minta -ing.
items.analogy_en: This **to** is in disguise: a preposition wanting -ing.
items.tip_id: Hafalin **to** yang minta -ing: look forward to, be used to, object to.
items.tip_en: **look forward to, be used to, object to** + -ing.

items.prompt: The ancient coins {A}that{/A} {B}discovered{/B} near the river {C}are now{/C} displayed {D}in{/D} the city museum.
items.why_correct_id: Koin nggak bisa nemuin sesuatu. Koin ditemukan orang, jadi butuh pasif: **that were discovered**.
items.why_correct_en: Coins don't discover; they are discovered: **that were discovered**.

why_wrong_id.0: **that** pas buat benda.
why_wrong_id.2: Pasif present **are now displayed** cocok buat sekarang.
why_wrong_id.3: **in the museum** kata depan tempat.

items.analogy_id: Koin itu harta karun, bukan pemburu harta. Harta karun ditemukan, nggak nemuin.
items.analogy_en: Coins are treasure, not treasure hunters.
items.tip_id: Setelah **that/which**, cek: pelakunya bisa ngelakuin aksi itu? Kalau nggak, pakai be + V3.
items.tip_en: After **that/which**, can it do the action? If not, be + V3.

items.prompt: The company announced that {A}its{/A} profits had doubled, so {B}the{/B} employees bought gifts for {C}theirselves{/C} and {D}their{/D} families.
items.why_correct_id: **theirselves** bukan kata yang bener. Reflexive pronoun (kata ganti diri) buat **employees** itu **themselves**.
items.why_correct_en: **theirselves** isn't a word. It's **themselves**.

why_wrong_id.0: **its** buat **The company**, tunggal. Pas.
why_wrong_id.1: **the employees** pakai article (kata sandang) **the** karena karyawannya jelas, milik perusahaan itu. Aman.
why_wrong_id.3: **their families** milik para karyawan. Pas.

why_wrong_en.1: **the employees** is fine; they are specific.

items.analogy_id: Kata ganti diri itu kayak cermin. Buat banyak orang, cerminnya **themselves**.
items.analogy_en: A reflexive pronoun is a mirror; for many people it's **themselves**.
items.tip_id: Hafalin: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves.
items.tip_en: Learn the reflexive set; **theirselves** isn't in it.

items.prompt: The new library offers {A}quiet{/A} study areas, {B}comfortable{/B} seating, and {C}it has{/C} {D}free{/D} printing for all students.
items.why_correct_id: Daftar setelah **offers** isinya kata benda: **study areas**, **seating**. **it has** nyisipin anak kalimat baru. Biar sejajar cukup **free printing**.
items.why_correct_en: After **offers**, the list is nouns. **it has** breaks it; just **free printing**.

why_wrong_id.0: **quiet** kata sifat buat **study areas**.
why_wrong_id.1: **comfortable** kata sifat buat **seating**.
why_wrong_id.3: **free** kata sifat buat **printing**.

items.analogy_id: Daftar menu itu nama makanan semua. Kalau satu baris tiba-tiba kalimat lengkap, aneh kan.
items.analogy_en: A menu lists dishes. A full sentence in one line looks odd.
items.tip_id: Daftar dengan **and**? Kalau satu anggota punya pelaku + kata kerja sendiri, itu salah.
items.tip_en: In a list, an item with its own subject and verb is wrong.

items.prompt: There {A}is{/A} still many unanswered questions {B}about{/B} how the pyramids {C}were{/C} {D}built{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: Setelah **There**, kata kerja ngikut benda sesudahnya: **many unanswered questions**, jamak. Jadi **There are**.
items.why_correct_en: **questions** is plural: **There are**.

why_wrong_id.1: **questions about** kata depan topik. Pas.
why_wrong_id.2: **the pyramids were** jamak dan lampau. Aman.
why_wrong_id.3: **were built** pasif lampau. Pas.

items.analogy_id: **There** cuma penunjuk jalan. Yang nentuin kata kerjanya tamu yang datang: **many questions**.
items.analogy_en: **There** points the way; the guests, **many questions**, set the verb.
items.tip_id: Kalimat **There + be**? Lompat ke kata benda pertama setelahnya buat cek tunggal atau jamak.
items.tip_en: **There + be**? Jump to the noun after it.

items.prompt: {A}That{/A} the Earth {B}moving{/B} around the Sun {C}was{/C} not widely {D}accepted{/D} until the seventeenth century.
items.why_correct_id: **That the Earth ... around the Sun** itu noun clause (anak kalimat sebagai kata benda) yang jadi pelaku. Di dalamnya butuh kata kerja lengkap: **moves**, bukan **moving**.
items.why_correct_en: The **That** clause needs its own full verb: **moves**.

why_wrong_id.0: **That** pembuka noun clause yang jadi pelaku. Pas.
why_wrong_id.2: Pelakunya satu noun clause, jadi tunggal **was**.
why_wrong_id.3: **was accepted** pasif yang pas.

items.analogy_id: Noun clause itu mobil kecil di dalam truk. Mobil kecil itu juga butuh mesinnya sendiri.
items.analogy_en: A noun clause is a small car inside a truck. It needs its own engine.
items.tip_id: Kalimat dibuka **That** + pelaku? Cek ada dua kata kerja: satu di dalam, satu di luar.
items.tip_en: Starts with **That** + subject? You need two verbs: one inside, one outside.

items.title: Why Zebras Have Stripes
items.body:
Few animals are as instantly recognizable as the zebra, yet scientists have argued for more than 150 years about why it has stripes. Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace, two founders of evolutionary theory, disagreed on the question. Since then, researchers have proposed at least a dozen explanations, ranging from camouflage to temperature control.

The oldest idea is that stripes help zebras hide. In tall grass, the vertical lines might break up the outline of the animal's body. Another version suggests that when a herd runs, the moving stripes confuse predators such as lions, making it hard for them to pick out a single target. However, studies of lion hunting have found little support for either idea. Lions hunt mostly at dusk and at night, when stripes are difficult to see, and they catch zebras about as often as they catch other prey of similar size.

A second explanation focuses on heat. Black stripes absorb more sunlight than white ones, and some scientists proposed that this difference creates small currents of air that cool the animal. Experiments with water barrels covered in striped hides, however, showed no clear cooling effect, and the idea remains **controversial**.

The explanation with the strongest evidence today involves insects. Horseflies and tsetse flies bite large mammals, drink their blood, and spread serious diseases. In one well-known study, researchers in England placed coats with black and white stripes on ordinary horses and filmed flies approaching them. The flies circled the striped horses just as often as plain ones, but they had great difficulty landing on them. Instead of slowing down smoothly, many flew straight past or bumped into the coats. The researchers concluded that the stripes interfere with the way flies judge distance and speed during the final moments of approach.

This finding fits with where zebras live. Species with the boldest stripes tend to be found in regions with the most biting flies. Zebras also have shorter hair than many other grazing animals, which may make **them** especially **vulnerable** to bites. If the insect hypothesis is correct, the zebra's coat is less like a disguise and more like a natural insect repellent, one that works not by hiding the animal but by confusing its smallest enemies.

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The hunting methods of lions in Africa
Competing explanations for why zebras have stripes
How flies spread diseases among horses
The scientific careers of Darwin and Wallace
questions.evidence_quote: Since then, researchers have proposed at least a dozen explanations, ranging from camouflage to temperature control.
questions.why_correct_id: Paragraf 1 bilang ada banyak penjelasan. Paragraf 2 bahas kamuflase, paragraf 3 panas, paragraf 4 dan 5 serangga. Jadi isinya berbagai penjelasan soal belang zebra.
questions.why_correct_en: The text weighs several explanations: camouflage, heat, and insects.

why_wrong_id.0: Singa cuma dibahas buat nguji teori kamuflase.
why_wrong_id.2: Lalat dibahas sebagai salah satu penjelasan, bukan topik utama.
why_wrong_id.3: Darwin dan Wallace cuma disebut sekali di paragraf 1.

why_wrong_en.0: Lions only test the camouflage idea.

questions.analogy_id: Main idea itu payung. Harus nutupin semua paragraf, bukan cuma satu.
questions.analogy_en: The main idea is an umbrella covering every paragraph.
questions.tip_id: Teks yang nyebut **at least a dozen explanations** di awal biasanya bakal ngebahas beberapa teori.
questions.tip_en: An opening that mentions many explanations usually reviews several theories.

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 1, what is true of Darwin and Wallace?
options: They proved that stripes are a kind of camouflage.
They believed stripes help zebras stay cool.
They were the first to study biting flies.
They disagreed about the reason for zebra stripes.
questions.evidence_quote: Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace, two founders of evolutionary theory, disagreed on the question.
questions.why_correct_id: Teks bilang mereka **disagreed on the question**, yaitu soal kenapa zebra berbelang.
questions.why_correct_en: They **disagreed on the question** of why zebras have stripes.

why_wrong_id.0: Nggak ada yang dibuktikan. Mereka malah beda pendapat.
why_wrong_id.1: Teori panas nggak dihubungkan sama mereka.
why_wrong_id.2: Lalat penggigit nggak dihubungkan sama mereka.

why_wrong_en.1: The heat idea isn't linked to them.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak dua juri yang nonton lomba yang sama tapi ngasih nilai beda.
questions.analogy_en: Like two judges watching the same contest and scoring it differently.
questions.tip_id: Soal detail yang nyebut nama orang? Scanning nama itu, baca satu kalimatnya aja.
questions.tip_en: Detail about a name? Scan for it and read that sentence.

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 2, why do lion studies give little support to the camouflage idea?
options: Lions avoid hunting in tall grass.
Lions catch zebras more often than other prey.
Lions usually hunt when stripes are hard to see.
questions.evidence_quote: Lions hunt mostly at dusk and at night, when stripes are difficult to see, and they catch zebras about as often as they catch other prey of similar size.
questions.why_correct_id: Singa berburu **at dusk and at night, when stripes are difficult to see**. Kalau belangnya nggak kelihatan, ya nggak bisa jadi kamuflase.
questions.why_correct_en: Lions hunt **when stripes are difficult to see**, so stripes can't be doing much hiding.

why_wrong_id.0: Rumput tinggi cuma bagian dari teori kamuflase, bukan kebiasaan singa.
why_wrong_id.1: Singa berburu sendiri atau berkelompok nggak dibahas.
why_wrong_id.2: Teks bilang **about as often**, kurang lebih sama, bukan lebih sering.

why_wrong_en.0: Tall grass is part of the theory, not lion behavior.

questions.analogy_id: Kostum kamuflase nggak ada gunanya kalau lawannya main petak umpet di ruangan gelap.
questions.analogy_en: Camouflage is useless if the seeker plays in the dark.
questions.tip_id: Kata **However** di paragraf sering ngenalin bukti yang ngelawan teori. Jawabannya biasanya di situ.
questions.tip_en: **However** often introduces the counter-evidence.

questions.prompt: The word **controversial** in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
questions.evidence_quote: Experiments with water barrels covered in striped hides, however, showed no clear cooling effect, and the idea remains controversial.
questions.why_correct_id: Eksperimennya **showed no clear cooling effect**, jadi ilmuwan masih berdebat. **controversial** artinya masih diperdebatkan, sama dengan **disputed**.
questions.why_correct_en: With **no clear cooling effect**, the idea is still argued over: **disputed**.

why_wrong_id.1: **popular** artinya disukai banyak orang. Teks nggak bilang begitu.
why_wrong_id.2: **proven** artinya terbukti. Kebalikannya, buktinya belum jelas.
why_wrong_id.3: **forgotten** artinya dilupakan. Idenya masih dibahas, jadi nggak dilupakan.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak keputusan wasit yang masih diperdebatkan penonton setelah pertandingan selesai.
questions.analogy_en: Like a referee's call fans still argue about after the match.
questions.tip_id: Ganti kata yang ditanya dengan tiap opsi, lalu baca ulang kalimatnya. Pilih yang maknanya tetap nyambung.
questions.tip_en: Swap each option in and reread.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the heat explanation?
options: It has been proved correct by experiments.
It explains why zebras have short hair.
It was first proposed by Darwin.
Scientists have not yet agreed whether it is correct.
questions.evidence_quote: Experiments with water barrels covered in striped hides, however, showed no clear cooling effect, and the idea remains controversial.
questions.why_correct_id: Eksperimennya nggak ngasih hasil jelas dan idenya **remains controversial**. Artinya ilmuwan belum sepakat teori ini bener atau nggak.
questions.why_correct_en: No clear effect and **remains controversial**: scientists haven't agreed.

why_wrong_id.0: Kebalikannya. Hasilnya **no clear cooling effect**.
why_wrong_id.1: Rambut pendek dibahas di paragraf 5, kaitannya sama gigitan lalat.
why_wrong_id.2: Teks nggak bilang siapa yang pertama ngusulin.

why_wrong_en.1: Short hair relates to fly bites.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak kasus yang belum ditutup polisi. Ada dugaan, tapi buktinya belum kuat.
questions.analogy_en: Like a case the police haven't closed: a theory, but weak evidence.
questions.tip_id: Kata **remains** + kata sifat sering jadi petunjuk inference: kondisinya masih begitu sampai sekarang.
questions.tip_en: **remains** + adjective says the situation still holds.

questions.prompt: According to the study described in paragraph 4, how did the striped coats affect flies?
options: Flies had difficulty landing on the horses.
Flies were attracted to the white stripes only.
Flies were killed by the coats.
questions.evidence_quote: The flies circled the striped horses just as often as plain ones, but they had great difficulty landing on them.
questions.why_correct_id: Lalatnya tetap datang, tapi **had great difficulty landing on them**. Jadi belangnya bikin lalat susah mendarat.
questions.why_correct_en: Flies still came but **had great difficulty landing**.

why_wrong_id.1: Warna putih nggak dibahas terpisah.
why_wrong_id.2: Kebalikannya. Lalat tetap mengitari kudanya **just as often**.
why_wrong_id.3: Nggak ada lalat yang mati. Mereka cuma lewat atau nabrak.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak pesawat yang bisa lihat bandara tapi lampu landasannya kedip-kedip. Bisa muter, susah mendarat.
questions.analogy_en: Like a plane that sees the airport but can't land because the runway lights flicker.
questions.tip_id: Hati-hati opsi yang terlalu ekstrem kayak **stopped** atau **killed**. Cek kata persisnya di teks.
questions.tip_en: Beware extreme options like **stopped** or **killed**.

questions.prompt: Why does the author mention the coats placed on horses?
options: To show that horses are related to zebras
To describe an experiment that tested the insect explanation
To argue that horses should wear coats in summer
To compare the diseases of horses and zebras
questions.evidence_quote: In one well-known study, researchers in England placed coats with black and white stripes on ordinary horses and filmed flies approaching them.
questions.why_correct_id: Paragraf 4 ngenalin teori serangga, lalu ngasih **one well-known study** pakai kuda berjaket belang. Tujuannya ngejelasin eksperimen yang nguji teori itu.
questions.why_correct_en: It's **one well-known study** testing the insect idea.

why_wrong_id.0: Hubungan kerabat kuda dan zebra nggak dibahas.
why_wrong_id.2: Nggak ada saran buat kuda pakai jaket.
why_wrong_id.3: Penyakit cuma disebut sekilas, nggak dibandingin.

questions.analogy_id: Contoh eksperimen di teks itu kayak foto bukti di laporan. Gunanya buat nunjukin teori diuji.
questions.analogy_en: An experiment in a text is the evidence photo in a report.
questions.tip_id: Soal **Why does the author mention**? Lihat kalimat sebelum contohnya, itu yang mau didukung.
questions.tip_en: **Why mention X?** Read the sentence before X.

questions.prompt: The word **them** in paragraph 5 refers to
questions.evidence_quote: Zebras also have shorter hair than many other grazing animals, which may make them especially vulnerable to bites.
questions.why_correct_id: Yang punya rambut lebih pendek itu **Zebras**. Rambut pendek bikin **them** gampang digigit. Jadi **them** = zebra.
questions.why_correct_en: **Zebras** have short hair, which makes **them** vulnerable.

why_wrong_id.0: Wilayah nggak bisa digigit.
why_wrong_id.2: **bites** muncul sesudah **them**, dan gigitan nggak bisa digigit.
why_wrong_id.3: Lalat itu yang menggigit, bukan yang rentan.

why_wrong_en.2: **bites** comes after and can't be bitten.

items.title: The Canal That Built a City
items.body:
In the early nineteenth century, moving goods across the United States was slow and expensive. The Appalachian Mountains separated the farms of the interior from the cities of the Atlantic coast, and shipping a ton of flour from Buffalo to New York City by wagon could take three weeks and cost about one hundred dollars. Many people believed that a canal linking the Great Lakes with the Hudson River, later called the Erie Canal, could solve the problem, but the distance, roughly 580 kilometers, made the project seem impossible.

The governor of New York, DeWitt Clinton, disagreed. After the federal government refused to pay for the project, Clinton persuaded the state legislature to fund it, and construction began in 1817. Critics called the canal Clinton's Ditch and predicted that it would bankrupt the state. Few of the people who designed it had formal engineering training. **They** learned by doing, and along the way they developed new tools, including a device for pulling tree stumps out of the ground and a kind of cement that hardened under water.

The work was **grueling**. Thousands of laborers, many of them recent immigrants from Ireland, dug the channel largely by hand, using shovels, picks, and horse-drawn plows. To carry the canal over rivers and up the slope toward Lake Erie, the builders constructed eighteen aqueducts and 83 locks, chambers that raise or lower boats from one water level to another.

When the canal opened in 1825, it was an immediate success. The cost of shipping fell by as much as 90 percent, and the travel time from Buffalo to New York City dropped to about eight days. Within a decade, the tolls collected from boats had repaid the entire cost of construction. Towns such as Rochester and Syracuse grew rapidly along its route, and New York City became the busiest port in the country.

The canal's importance eventually declined as railroads, which were faster and could operate in winter when the canal froze, took over most freight traffic. Even so, it had already reshaped the nation's economy by opening the interior to settlement and trade. Today, the canal is used mainly by pleasure boats, and its towpaths, where horses once pulled barges, have become popular trails for cyclists and walkers.

items.title: Painting on Wet Walls
items.body:
Fresco is one of the oldest and most durable methods of painting. The word comes from the Italian for fresh, a reference to the fact that the artist applies paint to plaster that is still wet. As the plaster dries, a chemical reaction with carbon dioxide in the air turns the lime in the plaster into calcium carbonate, which locks the particles of pigment into the wall itself. The image does not sit on the surface like ordinary paint; it becomes part of the wall.

This technique places unusual demands on the painter. Because plaster stays workable for only about six to eight hours, a fresco must be completed in sections. Each morning, a plasterer spreads a fresh layer over just the area that the artist expects to finish that day. These daily patches, called giornate, can often be seen by modern experts, who use them to work out how long a painting took. Michelangelo's ceiling in the Sistine Chapel, for instance, was painted in roughly 570 giornate over four years.

Mistakes are difficult to correct. Once the plaster has dried, the only way to change part of a true fresco is to chip it away and start again. Some artists added final details on dry plaster, a method known as secco, but these additions are far less durable. In many old frescoes, the secco details have flaked off, while the parts painted on wet plaster remain bright.

The choice of colors was also limited. Lime reacts with many pigments and can **alter** their color, so fresco painters relied mainly on earth-based pigments, such as ochres and umbers, that remain stable. A brilliant blue made from the mineral lapis lazuli was highly prized, but it was so expensive that patrons often specified in contracts exactly how much of it the artist was allowed to use.

Despite these difficulties, fresco remained popular in Europe for centuries, partly because it suited large public spaces. Churches, palaces, and town halls could be covered with images that would last for generations. In the twentieth century, Mexican artists such as Diego Rivera revived the technique, painting enormous murals of workers and national history on the walls of public buildings so that ordinary citizens could see **them**.

items.title: Where the Moon Came From
items.body:
For most of human history, the origin of the Moon was a matter of myth. Even after scientists began to study it seriously in the nineteenth century, they could not agree. Some argued that the Moon had once been part of a rapidly spinning Earth and had broken away. Others proposed that it had formed somewhere else and been captured by Earth's gravity. A third group believed that Earth and the Moon had formed side by side from the same cloud of dust and gas.

The Apollo missions of 1969 to 1972 changed the debate. Astronauts brought back nearly 400 kilograms of lunar rock, and laboratory analysis revealed two surprising facts. First, the rocks were remarkably similar to rocks from Earth's mantle in their chemical makeup, which made the capture theory hard to accept. Second, they contained very little water or other substances that evaporate easily, which suggested that the material had once been heated to extreme temperatures.

These findings led to what is now called the giant-impact hypothesis. According to this idea, about 4.5 billion years ago, when Earth was still young, it was struck by an object roughly the size of Mars, which scientists have named Theia. The collision was so violent that it melted much of both bodies and threw an enormous amount of debris into orbit around Earth. Over a period that may have been as short as a few years, this debris gathered together to form the Moon.

The hypothesis explains several **puzzling** features. It accounts for the Moon's dryness, since the heat of the collision would have driven off water. It also explains why the Moon has only a small iron core: most of the iron in Theia would have sunk into Earth, leaving lighter, rocky material to form the Moon.

Not every question has been answered. If the Moon formed mostly from Theia, as early computer models suggested, its rocks should differ more from Earth's than they actually do. Some researchers now propose that the impact was even more powerful than first thought, mixing the two bodies so thoroughly that their materials became nearly identical. Others suspect that Theia itself formed close to Earth and was made of similar material. Future missions that collect samples from deep beneath the lunar surface may help settle **the issue**.

items.title: Stripes at the Checkout
items.body:
Almost every product sold in a shop today carries a small pattern of black and white stripes. The barcode is so familiar that it is easy to forget how recent it is, and how long it took to catch on. The idea dates back to 1948, when Bernard Silver, a graduate student in Philadelphia, overheard a supermarket executive asking a university dean for help in finding a way to record product information automatically at the checkout.

Silver and his friend Norman Joseph Woodland took up the challenge. According to Woodland's own account, the key idea came to him while he was sitting on a beach, drawing the dots and dashes of Morse code in the sand with his fingers. When he pulled his fingers toward him, the dots and dashes stretched into thin and thick lines. The two men patented a design in 1952, but **it** was ahead of its time. Reading the code required a powerful light, and the lamps available then were large, hot, and expensive.

The invention of the laser and of cheap computer chips in the 1960s finally made scanning practical. Even then, the technology could not succeed unless the entire grocery industry agreed on a single standard. A code that only one chain could read was of little use to manufacturers, who would have had to print different codes for different stores. In 1973, after years of discussion, a committee of manufacturers and retailers chose a design proposed by George Laurer, an engineer at IBM, as the Universal Product Code.

The first product scanned at a checkout was a pack of chewing gum, sold in a supermarket in Troy, Ohio, in June 1974. Adoption was slow at first. Scanners were costly, and some consumer groups worried that shops would stop putting prices on individual items. By the early 1980s, however, the benefits had become **obvious**. Checkout lines moved faster, pricing errors fell, and stores could track exactly which products were selling, allowing them to order new stock more efficiently.

Today, barcodes are used far beyond supermarkets. Hospitals scan them to match patients with the correct medicine, airlines use them to track luggage, and libraries use them to check out books. Newer two-dimensional codes, which store information in a square grid rather than in a line of stripes, can hold far more data and can be read by the camera on an ordinary phone.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak colokan listrik. Kalau tiap kota bentuknya beda, pabrik charger bakal pusing.
questions.analogy_en: Like power plugs: if every city had its own, charger makers would struggle.
questions.tip_id: Kalimat **of little use to** nunjukin siapa yang dirugikan. Alasannya ada setelah koma.
questions.tip_en: **of little use to** names who loses; the reason follows.

questions.prompt: The word **obvious** in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to
questions.evidence_quote: By the early 1980s, however, the benefits had become obvious.
questions.why_correct_id: Setelah itu teks nyebut manfaat yang kelihatan jelas: antrean cepat, salah harga turun. **obvious** = **clear**.
questions.why_correct_en: The listed benefits were plain to see: **clear**.

why_wrong_id.0: **hidden** artinya tersembunyi. Kebalikannya.
why_wrong_id.1: **doubtful** artinya diragukan. Kebalikan dari **however** yang ngebalik keraguan sebelumnya.
why_wrong_id.2: **expensive** artinya mahal. Itu soal harga pemindai, bukan manfaat.

questions.analogy_id: **however** di kalimat itu kayak lampu yang tiba-tiba nyala. Yang tadinya ragu jadi jelas.
questions.analogy_en: **however** is a light switching on: doubt becomes clarity.
questions.tip_id: Kata **however** sebelum kata yang ditanya? Artinya biasanya kebalikan dari kalimat sebelumnya.
questions.tip_en: **however** usually flips the previous sentence.

questions.prompt: All of the following are mentioned as benefits of barcodes in paragraph 4 EXCEPT
questions.evidence_quote: Checkout lines moved faster, pricing errors fell, and stores could track exactly which products were selling, allowing them to order new stock more efficiently.
questions.why_correct_id: Antrean lebih cepat, salah harga turun, dan pelacakan penjualan semuanya disebut. Harga lebih murah buat pembeli nggak disebut.
questions.why_correct_en: Faster lines, fewer errors, and tracking are listed. Lower prices aren't.

why_wrong_id.0: Ada: **Checkout lines moved faster**.
why_wrong_id.1: Ada: **pricing errors fell**.
why_wrong_id.2: Ada: **stores could track exactly which products were selling**.

questions.analogy_id: Opsi yang masuk akal tapi nggak ditulis itu kayak tamu yang ngaku diundang. Cek daftarnya.
questions.analogy_en: A plausible but unlisted option is a guest who claims an invite. Check the list.
questions.tip_id: Di soal EXCEPT, jangan pilih berdasarkan logika umum. Cuma cek apa yang ada di teks.
questions.tip_en: For EXCEPT, check the text, not common sense.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the consumer groups mentioned in paragraph 4?
options: They were worried that shoppers would find it harder to know prices.
They wanted barcodes on every product.
They invented an early type of scanner.
They believed scanners would make checkout lines longer.
questions.evidence_quote: Scanners were costly, and some consumer groups worried that shops would stop putting prices on individual items.
questions.why_correct_id: Mereka khawatir toko **would stop putting prices on individual items**. Kalau harga nggak ditempel di barang, pembeli bakal susah tahu harganya.
questions.why_correct_en: No price on items means shoppers can't easily see prices.

why_wrong_id.1: Mereka justru khawatir, bukan minta barcode di semua barang.
why_wrong_id.2: Mereka nggak menciptakan apa pun.
why_wrong_id.3: Panjang antrean nggak jadi kekhawatiran mereka.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak takut menu restoran nggak nyantumin harga. Kamu baru tahu harganya waktu bayar.
questions.analogy_en: Like worrying a menu will drop its prices: you only find out at the till.
questions.tip_id: Inference dari kata **worried**: tanya, apa akibat buruk yang mereka bayangkan buat orang biasa?
questions.tip_en: From **worried**, ask what harm they feared.
